I have been playing this game for awhile, and here's some things everyone may be interested in...

A guy by himself, "Jam" has spent a year developing this game from scratch. He works on it daily, and updates go live daily. There is a client version coming out soon, which has improved performance and allows Mac users to play that can not play currently. This is on Steam Greenlight, and really needs votes!

The forum is an important part right now, because the developer communicates with everyone. If you make good suggestions, he puts them in. If you make good bug reports, he fixes them.

The game is not pay to win. You can pay a fee of $0.99 monthly in three categories. You can upgrade your starbase for more industry, you can upgrade your module allowance, or you can upgrade the amount of planets you can build on. You do not need any of these to play and achieve the same results as other players right now, believe me.

PvP is not introduced yet, but that's because Jam wants to make sure it works and is fun before he adds it.

The way the stars, gas giants, planets, moons, etc work in the game is the same as in Minecraft - they generate, and the engine allows up to 200 billion stars (solar systems) to be explored by players. Each star has moons and planets, and eventually asteroid fields that will be mineable, and you can eventually settle on any planet you wish... if it has an atmosphere. Otherwise, you'll need to work on a mega project of building a giant dome.

Probes were just introduced this week, and they allow a full diagnostic of a planet after a set amount of time. This means you will be able to have probes gathering information on any planets you wish, and you will know if they are good for any type of food or material gathering.

When you first start, you can mine / trade from station to station / scoop gas from gas giants / or pve to make credits. Contracts speak for themselves. You want to upgrade to a larger ship for more cargo space. Ships and modules that can be attached to them all work the same way, they are called classes. Example, I have a CL11 ship with a CL7 mining beam attached and a CL5 Ram Scoop.

When mining, don't burn the asteroid for too long or it blows up, you have to get the timing just right. When doing contracts, actually read them and pay attention. When gas scooping, certain colors and parts that are unique on gas giants are a good clue ;)

Before this post, myself and maybe 5-10 other people were active. As of right now it's hard for me to keep up with the chat bar in game because of all the new players.

Personal tips I would suggest, PLEASE register so your account stays open on the server. If you do not, and your PC crashes, you lose everything you worked for. After registering, look in the top right corner and read the wiki. It answers a lot of your questions. Go to Apollo, buy a starbase for 10,000 credits. Search other stations for a research lab and a warehouse for your starbase, they should be built asap.

From there, it's fun. It's free, I left Eve for this game. It's new, things come out weekly, and it's a 1-man team, be patient. You can do anything you want, you can explore anywhere you want. You can EVA and take a walk on a planet of a system you just discovered.

I should also add that right now, a huge update is being worked on and all of the old players are in a race to gather materials and do research before it is released. I won't spoil the secret, but if you start playing very soon and get established, you'll be one of the first along with us to be able to colonize the 200 billion stars in the universe. Oh, and build jumpgates ;)

Give it a try! Please support Jam also!

Don't forget to say hello in game when you see me :)
